items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: I was fortunate to work with Bill Watrous myself quite a bit... when we were recording the “Absolute Trombone” record

ctx.x: So among your projects, you’ve had “Trumpets 11,” you’ve had a project with seemingly every trombone player in New York in “Brass Nation,” 55 of the world’s finest brass players. So don’t you think you ought to try some big project now? I had a situation — some years ago I did my own record and I had Bill Watrous and Jerome Richardson on it. I had this weird feeling, like on a couple of occasions they weren’t exactly playing what I had written sort of exactly like I wanted it. But I had a hard time telling those…

Oh without question. And I think, you know, undoubtedly you approached it in a similar way. Like I just try to be — I try to express what I’m thinking and what I want to be different but I do it in a very respectful and nice, hopefully nice way. But I’m certainly, and I was fortunate to work with Bill Watrous myself quite a bit and, you know, especially people of my generation, Bill was a big time hero and you know, you just kind of naturally react to that. But there were a couple of times with Bill like when we…
Is there — with technology these days — is there a feeling sometimes that you’re giving it away for free?
